correction.text: the Pergamon fortress and its district under Philetaerus, three years before Cliopatria's first shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (-282..-280): the infobox dates Philetaerus' hold on Pergamon to 'approx. 282 BC' and the page has him rebelling against Lysimachus before 281; Cliopatria's first shape starts in -279. Same shape, three years earlier.

7.5 k km2 round Pergamon (27 cells), right for the Philetaerus years. Eumenes I's 261 gains ('land south of the Caicus to the Gulf of Cyme, plus garrisons such as Philetaireia and Attaleia') are small and probably inside the shape. The page gives no area before the c. 227 figure, so the area check starts with the -225 shape.

38.4 k km2 (131 cells; 105 beyond the old district). The page says the kingdom 'stretched over 143,000 square kilometres' after Antiochus Hierax's death (about 227): the shape is 0.27 of that figure, outside a factor of two; Attalus I 'gained putative control over all of Seleucid Asia Minor north of the Taurus Mountains' (Attalus I page), which the page calls tenuous, so the shape is taken as the secure part and the infobox figure as the claim. Gain dated 227 on the pages, Cliopatria starts -225.

correction.text: for -223..-213: the Pergamon district only ('shut up Attalus within the walls of Pergamon')

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria keeps 38.4 k km2 through 223-213. The pages say that after Seleucus III's murder in 223 'Achaeus then recovered the lost Seleucid lands and shut Attalus up in Pergamon'; in 218 Attalus 'retook his western territories' with Thracian Gauls but Achaeus returned in 217, and only after Achaeus was executed in 213 did Attalus regain his lands. For -223..-213 the kingdom is the Pergamon district (with the 218-217 swing recorded in the ledger).

38.4 k km2 again from 212 ('Attalus regained his lands after Achaeus was executed in 213'). The Attalus I page notes that Phocaea and Thyatira stayed in Seleucid hands. Aegina (acquired 210, base in Greece) is an island outside the shape.

176.0 k km2 (617 cells; 486 beyond the -212 shape, 478 of them inside the Seleucid -190 shape). Apamea: Mysia, Lydia, Phrygia and Pamphylia 'were given to Pergamon' (Pergamon page); the Eumenes II page lists 'the regions of Phrygia, Lydia, Pisidia, Pamphylia' plus parts of Lycia and the Thracian Chersonese. The shape also carries 124 Lycaonia cells (Konya) that no page opened names, and 22 Lycia and 4 Caria cells although Lycia and Caria 'went to Rhodes'. Infobox figure 143,000 km2 gives a ratio 1.23, inside a factor of two.
Unchanged (176.0 k km2); the pages record no border change between 188 and 133 (wars with Prusias I and Pharnaces I moved no frontier of Pergamon).
Unchanged (176.0 k km2); Attalus II 159-138 helped Nicomedes II to the Bithynian throne in 149 and fought Prusias II in 156-154 without border change.

correction.text: unchanged as a shape, but the state ends in 129: from 133 contested with Aristonicus' rebels

keyframe_review.note: 176.0 k km2, shape unchanged, but the kingdom ends earlier than Cliopatria's -127: Attalus III 'died in 133 BC, bequeathing the realm to Rome', Aristonicus' revolt ran 133-129 and Rome made the province of Asia in 129 (infobox 133-129). The shape is Pergamon to 133 and contested with Aristonicus 133-129.

region.text: the Pergamon fortress and its district, taken from Lysimachus's realm

ledger.note: 282: Philetaerus holds Pergamon. 'Took control of Pergamon around 282 BC' (infobox); before 281 he 'deserted Lysimachus, who held 9,000 talents in his care, and rebelled' and after Lysimachus fell at Corupedium in 281 'served the Seleucids with considerable autonomy'.

region.text: land south of the Caicus to the Gulf of Cyme

ledger.note: 261: Eumenes I defeats Antiochus I near Sardis and makes Pergamon independent. 'In 261 BC, he rebelled and defeated Antiochus I near Sardis, creating an independent Pergamene state'; gained 'land south of the Caicus to the Gulf of Cyme, plus garrisons such as Philetaireia and Attaleia'. The region is a 60 km radius round Pergamon, the reading of that land.

region.text: the lands beyond the Pergamon district that Cliopatria's -225 shape holds (105 cells, Aeolis, Mysia, Lydia, Ionia)

ledger.note: c. 230: Attalus I fights Antiochus Hierax. He 'fought Antiochus Hierax and his Gallic allies at Aphrodisium, in the east, near Sardis, and at the Harpasus in Caria'; the key battle is dated to spring 228 and the war to c. 230-227.

region.text: the lands beyond the Pergamon district that Cliopatria's -225 shape holds (105 cells, Aeolis, Mysia, Lydia, Ionia)

ledger.note: c. 227: the war ends. 'Attalus gained putative control over all of Seleucid Asia Minor north of the Taurus Mountains' (tenuous).

region.text: the lands beyond the Pergamon district that Cliopatria's -225 shape holds (105 cells, Aeolis, Mysia, Lydia, Ionia)

ledger.note: c. 227: Attalus I's gains from Hierax. 'Attalus gained putative control over all of Seleucid Asia Minor north of the Taurus Mountains'; the Pergamon page says the kingdom 'stretched over 143,000 square kilometres' after Hierax's death. Cliopatria shows only the 105-cell secure part from 225.

region.text: the lands beyond the Pergamon district that Cliopatria's -225 shape holds (105 cells, Aeolis, Mysia, Lydia, Ionia)

ledger.note: 223: Achaeus drives Attalus back. 'Achaeus then recovered the lost Seleucid lands and shut Attalus up in Pergamon', after Seleucus III was assassinated in 223. The counterpart is the Seleucid throne whose lands Achaeus 'recovered'.

region.text: the lands beyond the Pergamon district that Cliopatria's -225 shape holds (105 cells, Aeolis, Mysia, Lydia, Ionia)

ledger.note: 218: Attalus retakes the west. 'In 218 Attalus, with Thracian Gauls, retook his western territories.' The page names no places, so the region is the 105-cell extension.

region.text: the lands beyond the Pergamon district that Cliopatria's -225 shape holds (105 cells, Aeolis, Mysia, Lydia, Ionia)

ledger.note: 217: Achaeus returns. 'but Achaeus returned in 217'; Phocaea and Thyatira later stayed Seleucid. [Reviewer me-05-d, 2026-10-19: confidence lowered from 3 to 1: the Attalus I page says only that 'Achaeus returned from victory in Selge in 217 BC and resumed hostilities with Attalus'; it names no land lost in 217. The loss is a bridging reading of the Kingdom of Pergamon page, where Attalus 'regained control over his territories' only after Achaeus' death.]

region.text: the lands beyond the Pergamon district that Cliopatria's -225 shape holds (105 cells, Aeolis, Mysia, Lydia, Ionia)

ledger.note: 213: Attalus regains his lands. 'Attalus regained his lands after Achaeus was executed in 213 BC'; Antiochus III, allied with Attalus, took Sardis in 214 (Attalus I page).

210: Aegina. Attalus I was elected a strategos for 210/209 in the Aetolian alliance; the island was 'acquired by Attalus as his base of operations in Greece' and kept after the Treaty of Phoenice (205). The page does not say from whom.

region.text: the lands of Cliopatria's -188 shape beyond the -212 shape

ledger.note: 190: Magnesia. Eumenes II 'commanded the right flank at the Battle of Magnesia, which defeated Antiochus III' and took part in the naval battles; the Treaty of Apamea page dates Magnesia to 190.

region.text: the lands of Cliopatria's -188 shape beyond the -212 shape

ledger.note: 188: the Treaty of Apamea concludes the war. Antiochus III must abandon 'Europe altogether and all of Asia west of the Taurus Mountains'; the page gives the year, not the month.

region.text: Mysia, Lydia, Phrygia and Pamphylia (the Eumenes II page adds Pisidia, parts of Lycia and the Thracian Chersonese)

ledger.note: 188: the Treaty of Apamea. Mysia, Lydia, Phrygia and Pamphylia 'were given to Pergamon', and Caria, Lycia and Pisidia went to Rhodes, which later passed them to Pergamon; the Eumenes II page lists Phrygia, Lydia, Pisidia, Pamphylia, parts of Lycia and the Thracian Chersonese (footnote: Ephesus, Telmessus, Tralles); the Treaty page says Rome gave Eumenes 'a large part of Asia Minor' without a list. The pages disagree on Pisidia, so the region is Cliopatria's shape.

region.text: the coast (Leucae, Colophon, Myndus, Samos) and the interior (Thyatira, Apollonis) held by Aristonicus

ledger.note: 133: Attalus III dies and bequeaths his kingdom to Rome ('exempted Pergamum and the Greek cities'); Aristonicus, 'claiming to be an illegitimate son of Eumenes II', takes the name Eumenes III and revolts, seizing Leucae, Samos, Myndus and Colophon in sea raids and Thyatira and Apollonis inland. The seizures are dated only 'before 130', so the year is a bridging reading.

region.text: the coast and interior held by Aristonicus

ledger.note: 129: Aristonicus beaten. 'In 130 BC, Marcus Perperna replaced him and subdued Eumenes in their first encounter'; in 129 Eumenes 'was sent to Rome, paraded, and strangled in the Tullianum', and Aquillius divided the former kingdom.
129: Phrygia to Pontus. Manius Aquillius 'divided the former Pergamene kingdom among Rome, Pontus, and Cappadocia'; the Mithridates V page names the Pontic share 'the province of Phrygia'.

region.text: the share of Cappadocia, not located on the page

ledger.note: 129: Cappadocia's share. The page names Cappadocia as a recipient but no lands, so only the frontier strip with Cappadocia is marked.

region.text: the Pergamene kingdom, 176 k km2, annexed as the Roman province of Asia

ledger.note: 129: Rome makes the Pergamene kingdom the province of Asia. 'Rome annexed the former kingdom, which became the Roman province of Asia'; the infobox gives 133-129 BC, the text links the annexation to Aristonicus' defeat in 130.

wars.note: Key battle spring 228; Hierax supported at one stage by Ziaelas of Bithynia.

wars.name: War of Attalus I against Achaeus

zones.text: the lands beyond the Pergamon district that Cliopatria's -225 shape holds (105 cells, Aeolis, Mysia, Lydia, Ionia)

wars.outcome: Achaeus shut Attalus up in Pergamon (223); Attalus retook the west in 218, Achaeus returned in 217; Antiochus III took Sardis in 214 and Attalus regained his lands after Achaeus' execution in 213.

wars.name: First Macedonian War
wars.outcome: Attalus fought on Rome's side with a minor part; Aegina was acquired as his base (210) and kept under the Treaty of Phoenice (205).

wars.name: Roman-Seleucid War (Pergamene part)

zones.text: the lands of Cliopatria's -188 shape beyond the -212 shape

wars.outcome: Magnesia (190) and the Treaty of Apamea (188): Antiochus III gave up Asia west of the Taurus; Eumenes II received a large part of Asia Minor and Rhodes the rest.
wars.note: The war's opening (Thermopylae 191) is on the Apamea page; the Pergamene part is Eumenes II's command at Magnesia.

wars.name: Eumenes II against Prusias I of Bithynia
wars.outcome: 'He suffered an initial defeat, then won after Roman support allowed a counterattack' (183); no frontier changed.
wars.note: The Pergamon page dates the war c. 188-184.

wars.name: Eumenes II against Pharnaces I of Pontus
wars.outcome: Pharnaces 'sued for peace' c. 179; the land that changed hands lay in Galatia and Paphlagonia, not in Pergamon (see the Kingdom of Pontus dossier).
wars.note: The Pharnaces I page dates the war 181-179.

wars.name: Revolt of Aristonicus

zones.text: the coast and interior held by Aristonicus

wars.outcome: A first Roman army was defeated in 131, a second force beat Aristonicus in 130 and Perperna starved him into submission; Aquillius divided the kingdom among Rome, Pontus and Cappadocia in 129.
wars.note: Ariarathes V of Cappadocia, Mithridates V of Pontus, Nicomedes II of Bithynia and Pylaemenes of Paphlagonia opposed the revolt.

certainty.note: No treaty line is described: the Treaty of Apamea gave regions, not a surveyed frontier, so every frontier is soft.

notes: Pages: five opened (budget 5). Cliopatria rows: the -223..-213 shape wrongly keeps the 105-cell extension through Achaeus' war (corrected to the Pergamon district); the shape runs to -127 but the kingdom ends in -129; the start is -282 (infobox) not -279. The -188 shape includes 124 Lycaonia cells (Konya) that none of the pages opened gives to Eumenes II, and 22 Lycia / 4 Caria cells although the Pergamon page says Lycia and Caria went to Rhodes first; Rhodes' own dossier (eu-02) should carry the Rhodian Peraia. The Thracian Chersonese appears only on the Eumenes II page. Area: the Pergamon page's 143,000 km2 is tied to about 227 BC; against the -225 shape (38.4 k) the ratio is 0.27 and the shape is read as the secure part; against the -188 shape (176.0 k) the ratio is 1.23. Not settled: Pergamon's earlier tribute to the Galatians (Attalus I 'refused to pay them') is a Galatian-suzerainty relation recorded only here; Philetaerus' and Eumenes I's autonomy under the Seleucids (281-261) is a Seleucid vassal relation for the Seleucid dossier; the Galatian war of 189 (Vulso with Pergamene allies) is carried by the Galatia dossier; the 168-166 war with the Galatians is on no page opened. Needs a dossier: the Revolt of Aristonicus (Eumenes III), 133-129, is written by this batch as revolt-of-aristonicus (type rebel) from the same two pages; Lysimachus' realm exists as kingdom-of-lysimachus. Aegina is not in the gazetteer (a 30 km circle round 37.75 N 23.43 E is used).
